title: XiangShan Kunminghu core, CONFIG=DefaultConfig (generated from Chisel)
_note: XiangShan (香山) is the open-source high-performance RISC-V processor from
the Institute of Computing Technology (Chinese Academy of Sciences) and the
Beijing Institute of Open Source Chip.  The core is written in Chisel/Scala:
the repository contains NO Verilog, so this family runs the Chisel generator
first (see "generate") and sweeps the SystemVerilog it emits.  firtool runs
with --split-verilog, so the generator emits one file per module and the
per-module sweep works exactly as it does for a hand-written repository.
CONFIG=DefaultConfig is the COMPLETE Kunminghu core -- frontend, backend,
vector, MMU, L2 and L3.  Generated: 1980 .sv + 22 .v, 3.2 M lines, 2002
modules (~45 min cold for the Scala compile, 373 s warm, JVM heap 40 GB).
Reading XSTop needs ~36 GB of RAM for Surelog and ~11 GB for read_uhdm, so
this configuration is a WORKSTATION target, not a CI one.
NOT in the nightly matrix: see .github/workflows/sweep-ext.yml.  Run it with
The hand-written SystemVerilog arithmetic library the same project ships
separately is swept as the "xiangshan" family (XS-Verilog-Library).

cmds: PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH" NOOP_HOME="$PWD" make verilog CONFIG=DefaultConfig BUILD_DIR=./build

_modules_note: A representative slice, not all ~1900 generated modules.  The whole-core top
and the big blocks carry "want": "read" -- for them the question is whether
read_uhdm elaborates the design and drives every net, not whether a
multi-million-cell SAT miter closes.  The leaves are mitered against
read_slang and Verilator co-simulated like every other family.  The SRAM
macros are deliberate: a byte-enabled write to a dynamically indexed memory
is where read_uhdm used to expand one $mem into ~278000 cells.
